page.layout: One printed page (p. 286) with a single text column. A woodcut of an armoured soldier, with a suit of armour on a stand beside it, is set into the column's left half in the lower part, and text runs beside it on the right. Marginal reference notes stand in the left margin. Running head at top.

main_text.p: exuuias ferinas, ipsosque hiantes rictus capiti imponere. Apud Suidam scriptor: Οἱ δὲ πάρθοι τὰς κεφαλὰς τῶν θηρίων ἁρμόσαντες τοῖς πρανέσιν[?], ἐχρῶντο τοῖς τῶν θηρίων χάσμασι: Parthi capita ipsa ferarum galeis adaptan-tes, vtebantur earum rictibus. Statius libro III.

p.i: ——— ore ferarum Et ritu horrificant galeas.

main_text.p: Pag. 196. linea 2.„ Cristas aliquot è monumentis vide.] Non tamen hîc Polybianæ illæ expressæ, nec triplices. Polybij verba si quis attendit, dixerit magis pennas erectas fuisse, altas sesquipedem: cuiusmodi & Turcæ hodie gestant.
main_text.head: DIALOG. VI.
main_text.p: Pag. 203. linea 17.„ A Dousâ nostro emendatus, ærato.] Nec aurato tamen sperno: quoniam & loricas auratas lego, & Parthia metalli eius dives.
Pag. 209. linea 4.„ Exstat descriptio plena in libello qui Notitiæ.] Ne petere graue sit, en repræsento.

Pag. 210. linea 29.„ Librarum vtraque, an vtralibet? Ambiguum enim Plutarchi verbum, ἑκατέ-ρος. Sed magis est, de vtraque accipi, vt singulæ pependerint libras vicenas. Scribitur ibidem, solum Alcimum quemdam, valentissimum virum, centum viginti pondo armorum tulisse, cum alij non nisi sexaginta. Hoc ad omnia arma spectare arbitror: & nota olim eorum pondus.
main_text.head: DIALOG. VII.
main_text.p: „ Dextris cruribus.] Non vana sunt hæc Vegetij, nec mea quæstio.Pag. 219. linea 10. Sane pro eius mente funditor, quem expressi supra (in Dial. 1. lib. III.) sinistrum crus tectum palàm habet: contrà Legionarius, quem item expressi (Dialog. III. lib. III.) dextrum modò crus ferro tegit.

Pag. 222. linea 28.„ Sellarum equestrium fulcra.] Tale in Panegyrico Nazarij, quem Constantino dixit, vbi de Cataphractis equitibus ab eo cæsis: Tunc ire præcipi-tes, labi reclines, feminece vacillare, aut moribundi sedilibus attineri.

page.notes: The woodcut (soldier with spear, shield and helmet, beside a suit of armour on a stand) is an illustration and is not transcribed. Marginal references are the left-margin notes Pag. 196, 203, 209, 210, 219 and 222. The note placement for "Pag. 219" is estimated from its height beside the "Dextris cruribus" paragraph. Greek words "πρανέσιν" and the Greek accents are uncertain and marked [?]. Fragments of the facing page at the far right edge are excluded as edge of the neighbouring page.
